# E04 source audit 01 — VictoriaMetrics v1.134.0 vs ClickHouse TimeSeries v11

Status: **SOURCE-VERIFIED RESEARCH + REUSE OF VALIDATED LAB MEASUREMENTS** (2026-11-03). This is **not** a new runtime speedup, production recommendation, or new RNN claim. Scope: indexed label/time search, cache, cost-based filter selection, sample block access, and write amplification. No CI runs or new source patches.

Source versions: [VM v1.134.0](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/tree/v1.134.0) and [CH pinned 52529f0c711566d696917678bf15e7068772fdde](https://github.com/moleus/ClickHouse/tree/52529f0c711566d696917678bf15e7068772fdde). Actual earlier O1 CH reference binary: SHA256 `f0a2fa1f814c58853f43423705cac10ab9df3bfe5887e27ebe9620ba7cb9660e` from [build #41596421285](https://github.com/moleus/ClickHouse/actions/runs/41596421285).

## Executive findings

1. **Both systems already implement inverted label access.** VM writes tag-to-MetricID postings, including per-day and metric-name-composite keys. CH v11 TAGS uses `text(tokenizer='keyValuePairs')` for exact label matching. It is **wrong** to state that CH has no postings index. The main difference is **time scoping and plan integration**, not the mere presence of a postings index.
2. VM's index is **time-local**: it writes `(date,tag)->MetricID` for each series present on a day, searches days from the query window, and unions results. CH v11 TAGS is normally a persistent global `ReplacingMergeTree` ordered by `(metric_name,id)`; time information is in separate TimeRanges and SAMPLES. The CH native selector uses a TAGS/TimeRanges join to select IDs and then reads SAMPLES. [R19](https://github.com/moleus/ClickHouse/actions/runs/41635997049) confirmed the cost of retained TAGS/TimeRanges in one controlled scenario.
3. **VM has measured-work-based filter ordering**: it stores index-loop cost by (day, filter), sorts filters on that cost, and can switch the remaining filters to a direct metric-name check when their postings scans are too expensive. CH has generic SQL statistics and optimizer mechanisms, but its v11 native inner ID query explicitly chooses `full_sorting_merge` and `optimize_read_in_order`. There is **no source proof here** that its native path has an equivalent per-date feedback model.
4. Both systems group sample data by series ID. VM uses a TSID-sorted block/metaindex with time bounds per index block and block header; CH SAMPLES uses sparse `(id,bucket)` marks (default 256 rows, byte bound 524288). The **physical skip precision differs**, but a CPU advantage attributable to that difference is not established. [R05 mark study](../../experiments/R05_MARK_COVERAGE_FEASIBILITY_20261103.md) owns that measurement.
5. Optimizing SAMPLES alone cannot explain the full cost. [R15 valid native test](https://github.com/moleus/ClickHouse/actions/runs/41625086352) cut main SAMPLES marks 273 to 20 but broad native p50 only 67.98 to 55.45ms (1.226x); retained metadata rows dominated total read_rows. [R07 valid native/SQL test](https://github.com/moleus/ClickHouse/actions/runs/41634426255) got ~1.99x broad-pod 1d query speedup with **unchanged SAMPLES marks**. Read-plan and aggregation CPU matter as much as indexing for some queries.
6. VM's day index has a **write cost**, so do not transplant it without a break-even model. It must handle duplicate writes, long-lived series, late backfills, and consistency across replicas. Direct CH inner TAGS deletion is unsafe with a warm dedup cache ([R19 reproduction](https://github.com/moleus/ClickHouse/actions/runs/41642999590)).

## Two important source-derived algorithms

### A. VM learns per-date costs of matchers

From [VM `getMetricIDsForDateAndFilters`](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/blob/v1.134.0/lib/storage/index_db.go#L2516-L2721):

1. For each (date, label filter), load prior `loopsCount` and `filterLoopsCount` from an index-loop cache.
2. Sort filters by their estimated loops. Try a **positive non-empty** filter with low cost first. Postpone filters that exceed a loop/candidate limit.
3. Intersect or subtract the remaining candidate ID sets. Avoid parallel scans that would waste work after early reduction.
4. When the estimated cost of reading the next posting list is above `len(candidateIDs) * 150` *loop units*, apply remaining filters by checking metric names/labels of the existing candidate IDs instead. This is the source's fixed `loopsCountPerMetricNameMatch=150` [heuristic](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/blob/v1.134.0/lib/storage/index_db.go#L3066-L3067), **not milliseconds or CPU cycles**.
5. Stored per-filter loop estimates have a 3600-second freshness policy for relatively cheap filters, with exceptions for expensive ones ([source](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/blob/v1.134.0/lib/storage/index_db.go#L2530-L2550)).

Transferable idea for E03: runtime feedback for *label matcher evaluation*, independently from choice of `full_sorting_merge` vs HASH in the inner TimeRanges JOIN. This should be a held-out, same-query, source-pinned query-plan experiment; it must include estimation/update overhead and avoid per-user cache leaks.

### B. VM pays for new (date,series) entries on writes

[VM `createPerDayIndexes`](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/blob/v1.134.0/lib/storage/index_db.go#L2728-L2793) creates at least: (1) date→MetricID, (2) date+MetricName→TSID, (3) date+metric-group→MetricID, (4) one ordinary date+tag→MetricID per label, (5) one composite date+metric-group+tag→MetricID per label. The optional reversed metric-group path may add entries.

For `L` labels, the **source-derived logical insertion count** is at least `3 + 2L` per newly registered (series,date), excluding optional extra index rows. With 10 labels that is at least **23 logical insert entries** for the first active day; 14 distinct active days can cause at least **322 entries**. Merges may combine entries and the number of bytes or permanent rows does **not** equal this count. VM's same-day cache and next-day prefill reduce repeated registration and peak costs ([write code](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/blob/v1.134.0/lib/storage/storage.go#L2170-L2331)).

The correct read/write decision is a Pareto gate, not a read-only p50 win. For workload Q queries/time and P newly registered (series,date)/time, a rough CPU budget is:

`Q * (CPU_global_query - CPU_day_index_query) > P * CPU_extra_index_per_registration + CPU_extra_merge_per_time`.

This **is a planning equation, not a measured break-even**. Include extra storage, resident cache footprint, update consistency, backfill and replica behavior before selecting the index.

## Cache invalidation: additional source check

VM's tag-filter result cache is **not simply a permanent, never-invalidated snapshot**. The [indexDB constructor](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/blob/v1.134.0/lib/storage/index_db.go#L153-L193) passes `tfssCache.Reset` as the `mergeset.MustOpenTable` flush callback. The [mergeset contract](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/blob/v1.134.0/lib/mergeset/table.go#L338-L346) says the callback runs when a batch has become visible for search. [`addToInmemoryParts`](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/blob/v1.134.0/lib/mergeset/table.go#L911-L940) executes it immediately for a final flush, or schedules a coalesced callback. [The worker](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/blob/v1.134.0/lib/mergeset/table.go#L448-L468) runs on a jittered ~10-second tick when reset is pending. [DeleteSeries](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/blob/v1.134.0/lib/storage/index_db.go#L1554-L1614) explicitly resets the same cache on deletion.

**Implication:** a fair E02/R03 run must record `TagFiltersToMetricIDsCacheRequests`, `Misses` and `Resets` ([counter definitions](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/blob/v1.134.0/lib/storage/index_db.go#L202-L263)), and the relative timing of writes, flushes and queries. Turning off the VM **response cache** does not disable this index cache. A port to CH requires an invalidation/generation model that prevents false negatives on fresh and late writes, not just an LRU map. The code review alone does not establish a fixed duration of result staleness or its effect in the R03 benchmark.

| Test and configuration | Verified numbers | Meaning |

Cache may be warm. Not evidence that day postings alone cause the gap. |
| [R15 UTC-day vs monthly SAMPLES](https://github.com/moleus/ClickHouse/actions/runs/41625086352) | direct SAMPLES marks **273→20** and 70000→5000 rows for 1d; native broad p50 **67.98→55.45ms**, total `read_rows` **210000→145000** | Effective sample pruning, limited native gain. Remaining **140000 metadata rows** unchanged on this fixture. At candidate 145000 rows this is **96.6% of reported logical read_rows**, **not 96.6% of CPU**. |
| [R19 aged vs clean metadata](https://github.com/moleus/ClickHouse/actions/runs/41635997049) | 50000 retained vs 2000 live TAGS/TimeRanges, same 2000 live SAMPLES: **17x read_rows**, broad p50 **+42.8%**, CPU **+46.2%** | Real retained-metadata penalty on three runners. Not a safe TAGS-GC solution. |
| [R07 native vs SQL, held-out 2.49m points](https://github.com/moleus/ClickHouse/actions/runs/41634426255) | broad pod1d **70.20→35.20ms**, CPU **114.96→41.30ms**, selected marks **233→233** | Execution plan and label/grid work can dominate even with identical physical mark reads; restricted finite gauge oracle, not general PromQL fast path. |
| [R05 sparse mark range surrogate](https://github.com/moleus/ClickHouse/blob/lab/ts-cbo-adaptive-20261103/.github/ts-lab/experiments/R05_MARK_COVERAGE_FEASIBILITY_20261103.md) | Uniform-ID key-range model can select all 5208 mark envelopes although only 372 contain selected IDs | **Not native measurement**; explains why a smaller ID set does not imply fewer physical reads. |

## Prioritized action queue and epic ownership

1. **E03 (planner):** inspect VM feedback loop from `getMetricIDsForDateAndFilters`, compare with CH native `matcherToAST` plus SQL CBO. Design a *cheap-source* experiment: per-filter estimated posting scan versus direct candidate-label check; confirm per-query native plan reachability before C++.
2. **R07 existing owner (metadata time locality):** reuse VM day/date index source findings, retain full stable IDs and validate late writes, duplicate/day crossing, cache invalidation and write/merge cost. Do **not** introduce a parallel time-day sidecar under E04.
3. **R05 existing owner (physical marks):** compare actual CH `SelectedMarks` and matched-ID physical coverage on immutable parts. Do **not** use the R05 surrogate as an observed query gain.
4. **R03/E02 (cross-engine):** add VM `querytracer` per-day search, tag-filter cache hits/misses, `search TSIDs` and part/block counters to same source-pinned 1/4/8-client benchmark; compare with CH TAGS/TimeRanges/SAMPLES CPU and marks. Hold **same optimized build class** before ranking architecture.
5. **E01 integration:** require a pure source/config-controlled read/write/TTL Pareto gate before adding any schema/index change to the cumulative release-like stack.

## Open questions / explicit limits

- This review has **not** measured VM per-day postings cost, VM index cache hit ratios, CH TAGS text index CPU or VM physical blocks opened in the **same** trace. Earlier R03 profiling was not per-index causal attribution.
- We have **not** established whether a CH external cached filtered-ID-set exists and is safe under live ingestion: avoid an absence claim from limited code inspection.
- A per-day index may be expensive for stable, long-lived series; TTL, backfill and replica-safe updates are unresolved.
- Multi-column `tags_to_columns`, stats, projections and CH text index can help already; any VM-inspired implementation must beat them on equal inputs.
- The evaluated CH binary was O1 while VM benchmark was release optimized. E04 has not performed a fair production build comparison.
- Decision: **SOURCE_AUDIT_ACCEPT**, **NO_RUNTIME_GAIN_CLAIM**, **NO_NEW_EXPERIMENT_ROOT**. First independent practical gate is VM/CH cache-and-index trace collection, coordinated with R03/E02.
